args.query: Create MySQL 8 SQL for annual active employee headcount by gender, not annual hires. Cached similar query counts hires and is not suitable. Use dept_emp assignment intervals with from_date <= snapshot_date AND to_date > snapshot_date (exclusive end), and employees.hire_date <= snapshot_date; COUNT(DISTINCT employees.emp_no) to avoid double counting transfers. Generate annual snapshots with a recursive CTE from the earliest dept_emp.from_date year through the last observed historical date, defined as the maximum of dept_emp.from_date and non-sentinel dept_emp.to_date (exclude 9999-01-01 and dates >= CURRENT_DATE(), cap at CURRENT_DATE()). Snapshot is December 31 for completed years and that last observed date for the final partial year. Return year, snapshot_date, gender, active_employees with zero counts for both M/F where needed, sorted by year, gender. Do not extend historical data to current year just because open-ended records use 9999-01-01.

```sql
WITH RECURSIVE year_snapshots AS (
    SELECT 
        YEAR(MIN(de.from_date)) AS year,
        DATE(CONCAT(YEAR(MIN(de.from_date)), '-12-31')) AS snapshot_date
    FROM 
        dept_emp de
    WHERE 
        de.to_date <> '9999-01-01' AND 
        de.to_date < CURRENT_DATE()
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT 
        year + 1,
        DATE(CONCAT(year + 1, '-12-31'))
    FROM 
        year_snapshots
    WHERE 
        year + 1 <= YEAR(CURRENT_DATE()) 
),

active_employees AS (
    SELECT 
        YEAR(de.from_date) AS year,
        de.emp_no,
        e.gender
    FROM 
        dept_emp de
    JOIN 
        employees e ON de.emp_no = e.emp_no
    WHERE 
        de.from_date <= CURRENT_DATE() AND 
        de.to_date > CURRENT_DATE() AND 
        e.hire_date <= CURRENT_DATE()
)

SELECT 
    ys.year,
    ys.snapshot_date,
    COALESCE(a.gender, 'M') AS gender,
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.emp_no) AS active_employees
FROM 
    year_snapshots ys
LEFT JOIN 
    active_employees a ON ys.year = a.year
GROUP BY 
    ys.year, gender
ORDER BY 
    ys.year, gender;
```
